title_en: The Seat, the Samagam Text, and the Rosary
translation:
We cannot say with certainty in which year Revered Jagannath Maharaj established the gadi (spiritual seat) at Puniyad. However, with the aim of keeping the asan (sacred seat) preserved by Narsinhdas Maharaj in an orderly form, he cut an opening in his own sleeping room and set a door in front of it, making a small chamber. Inside it, on a marble platform, over two mattresses, he placed this asan and made it into a gadi. Further, Revered Shri Jagannath Maharaj placed some handwritten as well as printed books behind the gadi. In addition, some loving devotees from the community also placed certain handwritten manuscripts written by Ramkabir. Over time these booklets were removed and other scriptures were placed there instead. At the very start of the gadi's establishment, the texts titled Samagam (edited by Haridas Nadiad) and Harivansh Mahapuran were placed there from the beginning. At present, the scriptures on the asan (gadi) are, in order, as follows.

1. Harivansh Mahapuran — in the Sanskrit language with Sanskrit commentary, third edition, printed.

2. Samagam — editor: Haridas Nadiad, original edition, handwritten.

3. Uda Dharma Panchratnamala — edition 2, publisher: Revered Yadunath Maharaj.

4. Samagam — devotee Bhagwanbhai Dalabhai's copy made from the original, handwritten.

5. Dasratna Gita — contents: I. Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, II. Vishnor Divya Sahasranam, III. Bhishma Stavaraj, IV. Anusmriti Stotra, V. Gajendra Moksha, VI. Gita Sahasranam Shri Stavaraj Anusmriti, VII. Ram Mantra Patal, VIII. Ramchandra Stavaraj, IX. Ramhriday Stotra, X. Vishnu Panjar Stotra.

East:
1. Ramayan — by Valmiki, printed, publisher: Mumbai Press.
2. Mahabharat Ratnadarpan — short poems etc., Sabha Vanparva.
3. Girdhar's Krishnacharitra — Gokul Lila, Mathura Lila, Dwarka Lila, and so on.
4. Uda Dharma Panchratnamala — edition 3.
5. Bhagavad Gita — handwritten.

West:
1. Shrimad Bhagwat — in the Hindi language.
2. Bhaktamal — printed, Lucknow.
3. Uda Dharma Panchratnamala — edition 1.
4. Sakhi Parayan and Gyan Mahima.
5. Ramcharitmanas — pocket edition, Gita Press.

Haridas Nadiad composed the Samagam text in Shahpur, and it used to be kept at Jivanji Maharaj's original residence there. But the mother of Revered Jagannath Maharaj, Fulba, brought this text from Shahpur to Puniyad. It is said that Fulba, after a ritual bath with her clothes on, carried this sacred text and walked to Puniyad on foot, without wearing any footwear. Before Fulba, many attempts had been made to bring this text to Puniyad, but whenever it was moved from its original place in Shahpura, a fire would break out in it on its own; and when the text was put back in its original place, the fire would go out on its own. Thus the text could not be moved from its original location. But Fulba succeeded in bringing this text to Puniyad. After coming to Puniyad, it has not been taken outside the old and present premises. In Samvat 1939, when Jagannath Maharaj held the Shambhu Mela, this text was brought to Puniyad.

In addition, there is a tulsi (holy basil) rosary; Jivanji Maharaj used to offer prasad to the Lord (Bhagwan) using this rosary. Thus there are three sacred, worship-worthy objects at this place, and it was in this way that the worship of the gadi-asan began at Puniyad. Later, this practice was followed elsewhere in the community too, where gadi-asans were made and worshipped — at Surat (Begampura-Khangadsheri), Hansapura (now Bodeli), Darapura (now Vadi Vayadapol, Vadodara), Falu (Taluka Vijapur), Mumbai, and other places. At all these gadi locations of the community, handwritten books were kept on display for darshan (veneration). But this priceless and venerable literature has now been lost from all these places. Besides the asan-gadi at Puniyad, more than five hundred (500) ancient handwritten works are preserved in the Shri Ram Library.
